content_sections.body_text: Run can mean manage or organize: ‘Lan runs a club.’ Guests arrived for its meeting at 6:00 on Friday. Before then, Lan had run an event at school. Had run places the organized event before the 6:00 arrival. Write the two points on a timeline.
content_sections.title: Management before a past point

content_sections.body_text: In many accents, final consonant plus vowel can join: run_an event, event_at school. Keep /n/ and /t/ clear; timing varies by accent. Unstressed had may sound /əd/: ‘Lan [had] RUN_an event.’ Say it carefully, then smoothly. Clarity matters more than copying one accent.
content_sections.title: Two connected-speech choices

content_sections.body_text: A: ‘What had Lan run before guests arrived at 6:00 on Friday?’ B: ‘She had run_an event_at school.’ A: ‘How did that help?’ B: ‘She knew how to organize the club.’ Record A with pauses and answer as B; then switch. The goal is to recover the earlier event and its result.
content_sections.title: Ask, answer, and switch roles

content_sections.body_text: Make three boxes: what Lan managed; where; before what time. Record the talk, hide the script, replay, and fill the boxes. Check with this key: an event; at school; before guests arrived at 6:00 on Friday. Retell it, keeping run = manage and each weak form or link clear in your accent.
content_sections.title: Write, replay, and recover facts
